records.sourceFile: Acute effects of ad libitum use of commercially available cannabis products on the subjective experience of aerobic exercise - A crossover study.pdf

sourceVerification.doiVerification: DOI printed in the local PDF text.

records.evidenceSummary: Crossover laboratory study of 42 regular cannabis users (aged 21 to 39 years, mean 30.8) who ran on a treadmill for 30 minutes once after ad libitum use of a THC-dominant (n=31) or CBD-dominant (n=11) flower product and once without cannabis. Compared with the non-cannabis run, cannabis runs were rated higher for positive affect, enjoyment and runner's high symptoms (all P<0.001) and for exertion (P=0.04), with no significant difference in pain (P=0.45).
records.limitations: A laboratory crossover with no placebo arm, no performance outcome, and an unbalanced, quasi-randomized CBD group of 11, in highly active regular cannabis users who already used cannabis with running. The participants are healthy recreational exercisers rather than athletes; the paper is kept as exercise-experience evidence relevant to athlete substance-use conversations.
records.synthesisCaution: Reading the enjoyment and mood gains as a benefit of cannabis for exercise, or treating the THC and CBD differences as established, given an expectancy-prone design and only 11 CBD participants.

changes: populations: added Healthy Athletes, Male Athletes, Female Athletes (Table 1: 'Male 28 (66.7%) Female 12 (28.6%)'; 'Participants were therefore all healthy habitual exercisers')

Kept as INCLUDE because exercise experience and cannabis use are relevant to athlete wellbeing and substance-use education, but a reviewer may prefer EXCLUDE (c). Athlete tags applied by rule to non-athlete participants. Substance-use topic.
